r: In a follow-up submission, any service you remove is treated as cancelled. Keep every service on the approval so it can be processed at claim level.
Services sent with uncontracted codes are rejected. Follow the network protocol and submit new service codes three months in advance for analysis and feedback.
Emergency: no pre-authorisation before admitting the member — but the request must reach the payer within 24 hours of the patient's arrival in the emergency department.

If the eligibility response says no pre-authorisation is required, outpatient services are exempt regardless of cost or type — but inpatient admissions and every sub-limit benefit still need it: optical, dental, hearing aids, dialysis, autism, psychiatry, Alzheimer, circumcision, ear piercing, and maternity under the antenatal protocol.
The pre-authorisation threshold is shown in the eligibility response and is calculated on gross service prices per visit, excluding the consultation fee. Medication carries a separate sub-limit.
Inpatient extensions stay under the same approval reference. On the first day of a new month, submit a new approval number.
Daily progress notes are required for inpatient extensions.
Dental: request only the treatment that can be delivered in one appointment. Do not request the later stages in advance.
Dental: tooth number, attachments and radiographs are what allow an automated approval.
Dispensing a sunglasses frame and swapping the lenses for medical ones is recorded as fraud.
Chronic medication is submitted for 3 months, or up to the policy expiry date, whichever comes first.
Only standard devices with standard agreed pricing may be submitted.
Visit visa requests: the correct EMR form is required, the passport number or identifier must be entered in capitals, and every service needs prior authorisation.
Domestic helper requests: every service needs prior authorisation.
Post-assisted-pregnancy and IVF care is covered for CHI policies.
Normal delivery and caesarean section are covered where the caesarean is medically justified.
Once a pregnancy is complicated, every visit needs its own pre-authorisation — the protocol exemption no longer applies.
Aramco and SABIC accounts follow their own protocols; the Bupa protocol does not apply to them.
